chunks: And from him, from Sa'dan ibn Muslim, from Abu Basir, from one of the Imams (peace be upon them both)

Regarding a man who married off his slave girl to a man for four hundred dirhams, and he paid her two hundred dirhams immediately, then deferred two hundred dirhams to him. Then her husband consummated the marriage with her. Then her master sold her to another man. To whom belong the deferred two hundred dirhams?

He (peace be upon him) said: 'If he had not paid her the remainder of the dowry until he sold her, then there is nothing for him upon it, nor for anyone else. And if her master sold her, she has been divorced from the free husband, if he knew this matter. This proceeds from that principle, that the sale of the slave girl is her divorce.'
ai.seo_question: What happens to the deferred dowry of a slave woman if her master sells her before paying it?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the financial and marital status of a slave woman (*sarrirah*) when her master sells her before settling the deferred dowry (*mu'ajjal*). It establishes that the master retains the unpaid portion of the dowry as his right, and the sale itself constitutes an automatic divorce (*talaq*) from her free husband, provided he was aware of this legal precedent. This ruling highlights the distinct property rights of the master over the slave's marital bond in Shia jurisprudence.
